products.name: InternLM (Shanghai AI Lab)
products.note: Chinese open-source LLM; academic research; cross-border data review advised

reading.body:
Shanghai AI Laboratory is a government-affiliated research institution in China operating InternLM, an open-source large language model positioned for academic research across Chinese universities and scientific applications.

The laboratory's stated focus spans model capability, embodied robotics, and AI safety frameworks, with recent emphasis on science-oriented systems that integrate language models, specialist agents, and physical automation. This portfolio suggests a research strategy prioritizing broad capability development rather than any single domain constraint. The 2026 announcement of AI-for-science results and a scientific discovery platform indicates the institution is testing large models as infrastructure for experimental workflows, from hypothesis through validation.

What matters for AI infrastructure is that Shanghai AI Laboratory operates within China's university and research ecosystem, not as a commercial infrastructure builder or power provider. The laboratory contributes to model capability and research methodology but does not control the compute, buildings, or power grids that determine how quickly those capabilities can scale. It represents the downstream user of infrastructure, not the constraint that binds it.

The data does not cover the laboratory's budget, its access to compute hardware, or the power requirements of its training and inference systems. Without those facts, the connection between its research ambitions and the infrastructure constraints that may or may not enable them remains unmeasured.

profile_text.body:
Shanghai AI Laboratory is a government-run, non-profit artificial intelligence research laboratory in Shanghai, according to its own site. It recruits researchers worldwide in areas it lists as AI, large models, embodied intelligence, safe and trustworthy AI, AI for Science, basic platforms, the innovation chain, and management support, describing the aim as co-creating an AGI future. Since 2022 it has run a joint doctoral training program with more than ten universities, among them Peking University, Tsinghua University, Fudan University, Shanghai Jiao Tong University, Tongji University, the University of Science and Technology of China, and Zhejiang University.

Its tracked product is InternLM, described as a Chinese open-source large language model used in academic research, with cross-border data review advised. The site sets out a general-specialty fusion technical system in three layers: a foundation model layer, a fusion and coordination layer, and an exploration and evolution layer. It says that at the 2026 Pujiang Innovation Forum it upgraded and released a scientific discovery platform and fully opened its full-stack services, and that Professor Zhou Bowen proposed there that scientific research is the next programming. It also reports releasing W0, a physical world model, and Intern-Robotics, an embodied intelligence full-stack engine, and says that at the 2026 WAIC science frontier forum it and its partners released ten joint innovation results in life sciences, materials science, and deep space astronomy.

On safety, the laboratory describes an "AI-45 degree balance law" under which AI safety and performance should track roughly along a 45 degree line over the long term, and says it is exploring a causal path toward trustworthy AGI through three stages it calls general alignment, intervenability, and reflection. It describes risk management spanning assessment, training, foundation, application, and verification, and frames the goal as moving from making AI safe to building safe AI.
